'''Moana Lynore Mackey''' (born 28 February 1974) is a New Zealand politician and has represented the [[New Zealand Labour Party]] in the [[New Zealand Parliament]] from 2003 until 2014.  She has [[Māori people|Māori]], [[Irish people|Irish]], [[Scottish people|Scottish]] and [[Spanish people|Spanish]] ancestry.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

== Early life and career ==
Born in [[Auckland]], New Zealand, and raised in [[Gisborne, New Zealand|Gisborne]], Mackey attended Mangapapa Primary School, Ilminster Intermediate and [[Lytton High School]].<ref name="parliamentmm">{{cite web |title=Moana Mackey |url=https://www.parliament.nz/mi/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/mackey-moana/ |website=New Zealand Parliament |access-date=17 July 2025}}</ref> While in [[secondary school|high school]], Mackey would participate in [[Young Labour (New Zealand)|Young Labour]], the [[New Zealand Youth Orchestra]] and [[Youth Parliament]]. After leaving high school, she attended [[Victoria University of Wellington]] from 1993, graduating with a degree in [[biochemistry]] and [[molecular biology]]. Remaining in the Wellington area, she worked as a [[scientist]], leading a team at an environmental laboratory in [[Lower Hutt]] and from 2001 to 2004 was a member of the [[Petone Community Board]].{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

From 1999 to 2000, Moana Mackey served as President of [[Young Labour (New Zealand)|Young Labour]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Manning |first=Selwyn |title=Marginal Predictions: It's Turning Blue Out There |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/HL0509/S00166.htm |accessdate=21 October 2010 |work=Scoop |date=12 September 2005}}</ref> She also worked in the [[Trade Union]] movement.

Mackey entered Parliament on 29 July 2003 through the Labour [[party list]] after [[Graham Kelly (politician)|Graham Kelly]] vacated his list seat.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=20 July 2018|title=Moana Mackey joins mother Janet in Parliament|url=https://nzhistory.govt.nz/page/moana-mackey-joins-mother-janet-parliament|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-18|website=nzhistory.govt.nz}}</ref> Her mother, [[Janet Mackey]], also sat as a Labour MP until 2005 – the two formed the first mother-daughter pair in [[New Zealand House of Representatives|New Zealand parliamentary]] history. In the [[2005 New Zealand general election|election that year]], Janet Mackey retired from politics, and Moana Mackey contested but lost the [[East Coast (New Zealand electorate)|East Coast]] electorate seat (formerly held by her mother) to National Party candidate, [[Anne Tolley]] by 1,219 votes. However, she returned to Parliament as a List MP. Mackey unsuccessfully contested East Coast again in the [[2008 New Zealand general election|2008 general election]], losing to Tolley by 6,413 votes.<ref>[http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2008/electorate-10.html Chief Electoral Office: Official Count Results: East Coast.] electionresults.govt.nz</ref> Mackey again returned to Parliament as a list MP for the Labour Party.

Mackey was not placed high enough on Labour's list to return to Parliament following the {{NZ election link year|2014}} election to be allocated a seat following a drop in support for Labour. In February 2017, Labour list MP [[Jacinda Ardern]] won the [[2017 Mount Albert by-election]], which allowed the party to bring a new list MP to parliament. Mackey was the second-highest ranked Labour candidate not to enter parliament at the 2014 election. The person higher, [[Maryan Street]], announced she would decline the chance to return to Parliament. Mackey likewise declined the option to re-enter Parliament.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11804547 |title=Labour's Raymond Huo set to return to Parliament after Maryan Street steps aside |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=21 February 2017 |accessdate=21 February 2017 }}</ref>

== Post politics ==
Since 2015 Mackey has been employed in several advisory roles in [[Wellington City Council]]'s city planning team.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/dominion-post/news/98153727/councils-our-city-tomorrow-set-to-tackle-future-challenges-head-on |title=Council's 'Our city tomorrow' set to tackle future challenges head on |author=Devlin, Collette |publisher=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |date=23 October 2017 |accessdate=12 April 2019 }}</ref>
